what: The declarations the COMPOSITOR reads, and which are therefore load-bearing rather than cosmetic. `scripts/check-compositor-css.py` holds them. This is a RECORD, not a ratchet: the floors only come down through a diff line somebody justifies in review, and every required entry carries the reason it exists.
why: Deleting one selector from a group once took the whole `user-drag: none` block with it. Native image drag came back and swallowed the pointer stream — one pointerdown, two pointermove, never a pointerup — and three gesture holds failed for a reason that looked nothing like a CSS deletion. L07 converts 530 hand-written rules into utilities, which is precisely the operation that does this again.
taken_at: 2026-08-24, at the opening of L07, against the stylesheet before a single surface converted. RE-TAKEN 2026-08-25, at the close of L07, for two reasons and both raise the floors rather than lower them: the guard was counting its own PROSE (five of thirteen `touch-action` sites were sentences explaining the guard, so the floor could be met by documentation alone), and it was reading `styles/harness.css` — the instrument, not the product. Comments are stripped and the harness sheet is out; the figures below are the real sites, so a deletion has no slack to hide in.

required.why: THE INCIDENT. A picture inside a draggable surface starts a native drag that swallows the pointer stream outright, so every gesture built on pointer events stops arriving. Declared on `.tile img` and on the pressable group's images.

A mouse drag would otherwise select the text it passes over, which turns a swipe into a text selection. Declared on the pressable surfaces only, NEVER on the scrollport: it must stay possible to select the text of a synopsis or a release name.

The browser's own long press REPLACES ours rather than competing with it — no listener outruns the platform's menu. Without this the operator got « Copier l'image » where the panel should have opened.
Stops the scroll chaining out of the scrollport into the page, which on a phone reads as the whole app rubber-banding under the finger.

Reserves the horizontal axis for the swipe while leaving vertical scrolling to the compositor — the arbitration between a swipe and a scroll, made declaratively so the compositor honours it without a main-thread round trip.
The sheet's grab handle takes both axes: a drag on it is never a scroll.
Promotes the moving deck card to its own layer, so the drag follows the finger on the compositor rather than at the mercy of the main thread.

floors_note: `tap-highlight-color` is floored at ZERO on purpose, and it is the one entry that holds nothing: the prototype has never declared it. It stays in the watch list because it is compositor-facing and would be load-bearing the day one appears — a property with no floor and no site reads as an oversight, and a property absent from the list cannot be noticed at all.
